subject.title: fix(exec): stop isolated state dirs from moving live approvals

question: Should bare `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` remain a supported primary-state relocation with an explicit direct-doctor approval migration, or should every custom state root become permanently independent?
rationale: Current main, public docs, the related report, and the previously merged repair preserve direct relocation migration, while this PR intentionally replaces that contract with strict isolation and permissive missing-file defaults; only maintainers can authorize that security and upgrade-policy change.

options.title: Preserve relocation compatibility
options.body: Keep direct operator-owned migration and fail-closed runtime behavior for bare relocation while blocking named-profile, automation, temporary-state, and macOS cross-scope imports.

options.title: Retire cross-state relocation
options.body: Adopt independent state roots, but add a visible doctor migration/recovery flow and ensure existing restrictive policies cannot silently become `full`/`off`.

options.title: Narrow this incident fix
options.body: Land only the macOS and clearly isolated-scope repairs now, leaving the existing direct-doctor relocation contract unchanged pending a separate product decision.

recommendation.title: Preserve relocation compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep direct operator-owned migration and fail-closed runtime behavior for bare relocation while blocking named-profile, automation, temporary-state, and macOS cross-scope imports.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation, prior merged isolation repair, and this proposed policy change all trace most directly to this person's sustained work on the approval boundary.
